observation.visible_scene: A wide, eye-level landscape view of a rugged, partly snow-capped mountain range mirrored in a calm lake. Dry golden tussock grass and a small cluster of green shrubs occupy the immediate foreground along the bottom and lower-left edge; the mountain base/shoreline forms a horizontal band across the middle of the frame, with the inverted reflection filling the lower half.
visible_changes: The framing is essentially locked: the mountain ridgeline, the shoreline band, the left-edge shrubs, and the foreground grass tufts hold the same pixel positions from the first to the last frame, so no clear camera pan, tilt, or zoom is supported by the background.

The only visible variation is in the water's surface reflection, which shows faint, slow undulations that subtly warp the mirrored slopes over time; this is consistent with gentle ripples rather than any moving object.
The actual (non-reflected) mountains, the snow patches on the peaks, and the foreground vegetation show no discernible motion or deformation across the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the slight reflection changes are real wind-driven ripples or video-compression noise.
Any camera movement or change in wind occurring before the crop start or after the crop end.
uncertain_details: The magnitude of the water motion is very small and may be partly artifact.
A possible minor handheld camera shake cannot be confirmed, since the static background provides no clear reference shift.
